description: Read one list verification: the document version it checked, the list facts it checked against as they stood then, how each of those facts stands on the list now (held or included; its tier: `document` when a source is a document's record, `testimony` when its sources are only witness accounts, `unsourced` without a source; see lists.source-documents.update), and every claim found in the document with its verdict (state, and a 0-100 support score for supported, tension and contradicted), its qualifiers (caveats that never change the verdict: the record is not expected to speak to the point, a cited fact has a different scope, no document's record backs it and it rests on testimony, every fact it rests on is unsourced, or it rests on a held fact), the facts it rests on, for a record conflict the fact suggested to govern it (the document's record over a witness's account; null when neither), and the claim's current review (null while nobody has acted on it). A claim's `paragraph` is the printed number of the paragraph it sits in (null when the document's numbering is unclear or the claim is outside a numbered paragraph). Each claim's `staleness` says why its grade may no longer stand on the list as it is now: a fact the grade cites was edited (`fact-changed`), held out of scoring (`fact-held`) or taken off the list (`fact-removed`), or a fact the grade never read bears on the claim (`new-fact-related`: linked to it, from a cited fact's document, or on its words); empty when none of these was found (a new fact on the claim's point in other words is not detected), null when the list holds more facts than one check reads. Nothing is graded again until asked: re-check those claims with lists.verifications.claim-rechecks.bulk.create. `assertedOn` is the date the claim's words give (`dated`, with a `day`, `month` or `year` precision stored as its first day and its `source`: the words, or the grader when they name no complete date), or `none`. `carryOver` says what the run took from the previous run of the same document and list. Notes and fact links follow a claim with the same words or with edited words in the same paragraph or page; other decisions follow only the same words with an unchanged verdict. It counts the reviewed claims that came across whole and lists the rest (`text-changed`, `verdict-changed`, `unmatched`, `ambiguous`); null when there was nothing to carry. `unreadParts` lists the text a completed run could not read (each from `start` to `end`, a block id and an offset): no claim was looked for there, so verify the document again to read it; empty when the run read everything.
